# Independent Unit 1/2 review of Recording A

**Verdict: protocol and source identity PASS; causal budget and physical selection HOLD.** The successful matrix contains 24 pages: original, diagnostic probes off, probes on, and count mode for native and React at 128, 1,024 and 10,000 rows. Each page has 60 warmup and 240 measured frames. The original qualified 30-page comparison remains `QUALIFICATION_FAIL_DATA_VERIFIED`; these later single-page diagnostics do not replace its paired speed verdict. The analyzers correctly return `DIAGNOSTIC`, `decisionGrade: false`. No production runtime/compiler change, physical plan, threshold or speed claim follows from this matrix.

This is a read-only review. I inspected the [project rules](../../../AGENTS.md), [checkpoint](../../../implementation-checkpoint.md), [master guide](../../../final-master-plan.md), the four recording reports, their native/React analysis JSON and independent verifiers, the 24 successful raw `record.json` files, source/build/served-asset locks and source maps, the archived diagnostic Root/World/VDOM/compiler seams, and the [candidate proof map](../candidate-proof-map/report.md). The failed first native 128 attempt remains preserved separately; it did not contribute a page to the successful 24-page matrix. I wrote only this report.

## What is established

- All 24 successful records have the expected arm/size/mode, pinned Node 24.18.0 and headless Chromium 153.0.8010.12, production mode, cross-origin isolation, 60+240 frames, passing output/order/identity/lifecycle/dead-setter/visibility checks, zero page and cleanup errors, and matched served asset hashes. The independent verifiers report all eight records passing at 1,024 and 10,000; both four-page 128 pilots pass. Owned previews were stopped without disturbing shared routes. See [128 native](../native-128-pilot-attempt2/independent-verification.json), [128 React](../react-128-pilot/independent-verification.json), [1,024](../recording-1024/independent-verification.json), and [10,000](../recording-10000/independent-verification.json).
- Original pages serve the frozen build04 assets. Diagnostic off/on/count share one different archived-source build with source manifest SHA-256 `f1d274b68e6bfbbea3151aa57388bb90a9c8b6c1aa62914924aaba14e0b3e57f` and build lock `68fefba20876c02c0e2013699c64d4b31eb4deb6d02b3abbacb2fde09f798372`. Its native compiler component/program/site/slot/sink identity matches the original proof (identity SHA-256 `17acfbfa1e1ebbd6b44fd2594633e92daaac3af412efafcc3075f8e3182fe579`); React Compiler assertions and source maps are present. Original and diagnostic *asset bytes differ*, as expected. The source map contains the archived `owner_state_world.ts`, `pending_state_changes.ts`, `world_dirty_journal.ts`, Root, VDOM, DOM writer, both authored arms and React Compiler runtime. This supports semantic/source mapping, not equal optimized machine code or zero build-shape cost. [Build lock](../build-lock.json), [source manifest](../source-manifest.json), [qualified receipt](../../../results/current-owner-kernel-headless-v1/receipt.json).
- The `on` pages have 23 ordered native marks or 6 ordered React marks per frame, contained inside the timed commit, with zero invalid intervals. Native `q = on total − sum(exclusive intervals)` is nonnegative; medians are 0.010, 0.020 and 0.120 ms by size. React q medians are 0.005, 0.005 and 0.005 ms. This is a useful accounting audit; q still contains unassigned work, mark/timer effects and rounding. The native validation interval **includes reached dependency gathering**; host/equality includes output selection, writer wrapper and DOM writes. React's postdispatch interval includes render, scheduling, commit and host application. None is an isolated removable cost or host floor.
- Separate count pages confirm exact workload cardinality. Across 240 frames, native row callback counts are 30,720 / 245,760 / 2,400,000; each callback invokes **three** actual state setters. Input cells, VDOM inputs, staged outputs, host writes and acknowledged cells are 92,160 / 737,280 / 7,200,000. Thus this fixture has 3 changed host props per row per frame and no equal-output elimination in its measured frames. Count mode does not contribute phase time. [1,024 analysis](../recording-1024/native-analysis.json), [10,000 analysis](../recording-10000/native-analysis.json), [proof map](../candidate-proof-map/report.md).

## Actual timing matrix and why it is diagnostic

Each cell below is **one page** with 240 serial frames. Median/p95 are milliseconds. Signed deltas are from matching frame positions in different pages and include page, ordering, browser and build effects; they are not paired causal treatment effects.

| Rows | Arm | Original total | Off total | On total | Off−original median / p95 | On−off median / p95 | q median |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | native | 0.4125 / 0.580 | 0.295 / 0.385 | 0.335 / 0.465 | −0.110 / +0.005 | +0.055 / +0.210 | 0.010 |
| 128 | React | 0.285 / 0.385 | 0.375 / 0.990 | 0.255 / 0.325 | +0.0825 / +0.670 | −0.125 / −0.005 | 0.005 |
| 1,024 | native | 1.750 / 1.920 | 1.7125 / 1.935 | 1.6775 / 1.820 | −0.0325 / +0.220 | −0.050 / +0.160 | 0.020 |
| 1,024 | React | 1.4075 / 1.645 | 1.250 / 1.375 | 1.250 / 1.360 | −0.150 / +0.020 | −0.0025 / +0.170 | 0.005 |
| 10,000 | native | 21.853 / 23.120 | 21.200 / 22.545 | 20.833 / 22.960 | −0.657 / +0.920 | −0.377 / +2.000 | 0.120 |
| 10,000 | React | 14.405 / 22.130 | 15.295 / 22.160 | 14.210 / 20.915 | +0.865 / +7.295 | −1.113 / +4.335 | 0.005 |

The 10,000-row signed `on−off` frame differences range from **−9.150 to +7.065 ms native** and **−10.565 to +13.330 ms React**. An `on` page cannot literally obtain a negative probe cost from its timestamp calls; those negatives demonstrate confounding by independent page state, JIT/build shape, browser scheduling and run drift. The mode order at 1,024 and 10,000 was original/native, original/React, then native off/on/count, then React off/on/count. It was neither randomized nor counterbalanced. At 128, the two four-page pilots were collected separately. The fresh original pages are controls for source identity and contemporary totals, not a new registered speed study: there is only one page per arm/size, rather than five paired replications.

The independent unit for latency inference is the **page/block**, not each frame. Frames share mount state, JIT tier, heap, code cache, thermal/browser state and RAF history. The raw records show material within-page lag-one autocorrelation: for example native `on` is approximately 0.70 at 128, 0.66 at 1,024 and 0.33 at 10,000; React `on` is approximately 0.76, 0.48 and 0.17. First-half versus second-half medians also shift (native `on` 1,024: 1.690 to 1.670 ms; native `on` 10,000: 20.718 to 20.918 ms). The 240 frames are excellent for a page distribution and mark audit but cannot create 240 independent probes of build-shape or overhead. Matching frame 61 in one page to frame 61 in another does not restore randomization. A frame-level p95 of signed differences is not the difference of independent p95s and supplies no confidence bound on overhead.

The observed timer quantum is about 0.005 ms; the five-tick phase floor is 0.025 ms. Total commits clear the floor. React dispatch at 128 has median **0.025 ms**, at the floor, and some observations below it. Native capture, stage setup, mirror/cleanup at 128 and stage setup at 10,000 also approach or cross it. A rounded 0.000 ms median stage interval means unresolved under this clock, not free work. Even long phases are measured in a diagnostic build whose off/on controls drift. Negative median `on−off` at 1,024 and 10,000 cannot be interpreted as a beneficial probe or subtracted from phase times.

## Phase magnitudes: location, not removable share

The table is median milliseconds from each single `on` page. The parenthesized percentage divides a phase median by that page's total median **only as a descriptive scale**; medians of separate distributions do not form an additive causal decomposition. Exact phase marks and raw batches are in the `on` records. React's internals remain combined.

| Phase | Native 128 | Native 1,024 | Native 10,000 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Dispatch, including authored callbacks and World/Root notifications | 0.090 (27%) | 0.515 (31%) | 6.745 (32%) |
| Capture | 0.005 | 0.015 | 0.290 |
| World row/token resolution | 0.030 | 0.145 | 1.915 (9%) |
| Packed validation **and dependency gather** | 0.025 | 0.115 | 1.700 (8%) |
| Stage setup and source mirror | 0.005 combined medians | 0.015 combined medians | 0.295 combined medians |
| Generated kernel | 0.025 | 0.115 | 1.080 (5%) |
| Postkernel verification/staging | 0.015 | 0.075 | 1.320 (6%) |
| Host/equality/wrapper and actual style writes | 0.100 (30%) | 0.485 (29%) | 4.970 (24%) |
| Cleanup | below/near floor | 0.005 | 0.040 |
| Root accepted history and exact acknowledgement | 0.030 (9%) | 0.170 (10%) | 2.340 (11%) |
| React dispatch / unresolved internals | 0.025 / 0.230 | 0.140 / 1.100 | 1.340 / 12.835 |

At 10,000, native dispatch is the largest marked phase, but React does more of its work *after* setter callback return inside `flushSync`; the 6.745 versus 1.340 ms dispatch labels do not compare equal algorithmic obligations. The native host/equality phase contains **30,000 required changed style writes per frame**, so 4.970 ms is not removable. Root acknowledgement advances accepted per-root values and clears only captured versions from both World and Root pending ledgers; its 2.340 ms is not a licence to delete history. The generated kernel's 1.080 ms is comparatively small, making an arithmetic-only rewrite a weak single-phase candidate even if the diagnostic magnitude transfers. At 1,024/10,000 the diagnostic dispatch gross shares (31%/32%) are below the registered 0.8 reductions (39.5%/46.5%); even an impossible complete removal of that one phase would not suffice at those sizes. This is a prioritization clue, **not** a validated Amdahl ceiling, because diagnostic controls have not bounded source/probe drift and some dispatch work is mandatory.

The immutable qualified paired ratios remain 1.0637 / 1.3224 / 1.4963, requiring native reductions of 6.0% / 24.4% / 33.2% for parity or 24.8% / 39.5% / 46.5% for an individual 0.8 ratio, with the React denominator fixed. The strong-win gate needs two sizes; neither this matrix nor a gross sum of dispatch+resolution+validation+ack demonstrates those savings. For an eventual candidate `j`, compute a **page-level** lower/upper bound on removable work `R_j`, subtract required work and add new capture/selection/retention/host costs `δ_j`; only `T'_j ≥ T−R_j+δ_j` and a bound entirely on one side of the appropriate gate can support selection. There is currently no decision-grade `R_j`.

Cold mount/frame-zero at 10,000 was 274.700 ms native versus 55.095 ms React on the fresh original pages, approximately a 220 ms observed gap. It is a composite setup/mount/initialization interval, one page per arm, not a compiler-only or paired causal estimate. It is large enough that any later warm update saving must be checked against a realistic reuse horizon and retained memory. At 128, fresh original cold was 14.810 versus 7.660 ms; at 1,024, the original raw records must be used for cold comparison rather than assuming linear scaling. The existing allocation collector has **not** run: its 240 immediate all-dirty commits after warmup and 32 KiB HeapProfiler sampling cadence differ from RAF latency pages. When run later, it can identify allocation origins and retention hypotheses, not exact bytes/update or GC pauses in these timed frames.

## Source obligations that constrain a candidate

The archived source used in diagnostics is the same baseline family as build04, with marks only; the live postbaseline adjacent-token cache is absent and remains unqualified. [Candidate proof map](../candidate-proof-map/report.md) records exact lines. The following distinctions decide what can be removed:

1. The setter route in [World `#dispatchState`](../snapshot/src/owner_state_world.ts) at 2050–2140 checks owner life, evaluates a possible functional updater (user code), rejects a destruction during that callback, compares `Object.is`, promotes numeric lanes if necessary, advances cell/source/row lease and version, marks WorldDirtyJournal, then notifies a captured dirty-listener list and optional public change listeners. The Root listener at [965–995](../snapshot/src/component_state_runtime.ts) calls `world.isWithin` and `PendingStateChanges.setCell`, then schedules. [`isWithin`](../snapshot/src/owner_state_world.ts) at 1944–1953 walks parent links, so dispatch includes hierarchy work dependent on owner depth and subscribed roots. [`PendingStateChanges.setCell`](../snapshot/src/pending_state_changes.ts) at 43–63 coalesces by exact cell identity and version. None of this is generic “lookup overhead”: correctness and public notification ordering occupy part of the span. A direct Root shortcut must preserve multiple roots, grafts, owner retirement, functional updater/reentry, public subscribers and exact pending cuts, or be restricted to a compiler-owned closed path with a proven fallback.
2. `#tryCommitNativeRows` resolves every World row/lease/version and packs a Root-owned cut; [VDOM `#executePreparedNumericRows`](../snapshot/src/vdom_snapshot_runtime.ts) then validates caller arrays/token/source/column leases, gathers untouched dependencies, mirrors `ScalarSource.value`, executes the generated kernel, verifies output indices/masks/primitive values, writes hosts, and cleans scratch. Root acknowledges accepted source history, World dirty journal and Root pending keys only after successful host work. The two journals have different authorities: global World dirty state and per-root pending view. Merging them by name alone would break forks or newer reentrant actions. The 7.2 million acknowledgements at 10,000 are obligatory versioned observations, though their physical representation may be changed with proof.
3. The Rust emitter proves a narrow closed primitive syntax for *its emitted expression*, and the diagnostic build matches original program/site identities. But exported `defineComponent`, `bindSources`, structural metadata and `associateCompiledOwnerUpdateProgram` accept functions/objects by shape; current registration does not prove an arbitrary supplied `executeCut` is compiler-emitted, pure or nonescaping. The VDOM method accepts caller-provided arrays. A private Root cut can support a **closed-path optimization under a documented conforming-caller and internal provenance contract**; it is not a security certificate for arbitrary JavaScript functions or TypeScript brands. Preserve public path checks and fallback. A trusted internal compiler registry/module-revision mechanism would need its own escape/HMR proof before deleting output verification or leases.
4. The `ScalarSource.value` mirror is currently performed before projections and host writes. Exported scalar sources/bindings and generic projectors may observe it, especially on fallback, callback or exception boundaries. No present recording proves mirror stores are semantically removable. The public later-getter lease counterexample still forbids deleting the second live validation. The accepted-root source cache is a distinct visible frontier and cannot be removed merely because current World/source values exist. Host writers can partially apply then throw; no exact rollback or cross-host visual atomicity follows from this numeric path.

## One ranked, finite next step

**Run one targeted, counterbalanced dispatch-family control recording on the archived baseline.** Dispatch is the largest marked nonhost phase and part of any plausible multi-phase vertical candidate. The immediate uncertainty is whether its 1,024/10,000 marked scale survives source/probe controls; a sampled profile or allocation capture alone cannot answer that. Do not put `on` and `off` branches in the same hot page to “pair” frames: the toggle would change branch/JIT/heap behavior and still lack original-build equivalence. Keep the existing separate-page original/off/on modes and exact semantics.

Protocol: use **six independent fresh-page blocks per size** at 1,024 first, then 10,000 only if the 1,024 source/mark/control checks pass. Within each size, balance all six orders of `(original, off, on)` once, with their order chosen by a predeclared seed. The native-only design is 18 pages at 1,024 and at most 18 more at 10,000, all with 60 warmup and 240 measured frames; no count rerun is needed because the first count pages passed. React pages are excluded from this targeted causal-control rerun; the original registered React denominator remains fixed. Each page retains the original source/build lock or identical diagnostic build/served hashes, native compiler identity, source-map coverage, headless Chromium/Node context, output/lifetime checks and Portless cleanup. Preserve every block, including slow pages and failures. Predeclare the exact order and stop after these blocks; no adaptive search for a favorable run.

Analyze **page medians/p95 and block-level differences**, not 240 frame-position differences as independent samples. Report per-block `off−original` (build/environment) and `on−off` (probe plus environment), direction/range and a conservative uncertainty envelope across blocks. A dispatch phase is usable as a gross-cost bound only if that envelope is narrow enough that its lower/upper interpretation does not straddle the registered decision threshold after necessary work and new overhead. If controls remain unstable, mark causal budget **unresolved and stop this hotspot after its one targeted rerun**. If stable, combine the marked dispatch span with a read-only obligation map and already counted `U/r/W`; classify what must remain. Do **not** claim the whole dispatch interval removable. A subsequent implementation candidate would still require its own net-benefit, cold/memory and semantic qualification under Unit 2; the control recording alone cannot approve it.

The conditional candidate family worth reviewing, **only if the controlled budget is large enough**, is a single compiler-owned World→Root→VDOM numeric cut that replaces named repeated per-cell route/row coordination and preserves one exact per-root acknowledgement. Its old mechanisms to retire must be explicit (for example a Root listener/queue traversal or duplicate row/token resolution for eligible cells), while World public subscribers, hierarchy/graft routing, `Object.is` and updater semantics, live version/lease checks, source visibility, host write order and public/generic fallback remain. Adding a second dirty registry or merely moving the same O(U) work into an owned buffer cannot meet the budget. The candidate must separately show how 1,024 and 10,000 reductions can reach 39.5% and 46.5% where those sizes are chosen for the two-of-three gate, including new overhead; an isolated cache hit rate or current gross phase sum is insufficient.

**Decision now:** approve the data as a faithful diagnostic map; do not approve sparse/cluster/dense switching, a new row cut, B+ tree, SoA conversion, worker/Wasm backend, host-writer bypass, source mirror deletion, history deletion or adjacent-token speed claim. The one targeted control above is the next finite Unit 1 action. If it fails to bound the dispatch-family budget, Unit 2 reports HOLD rather than opening an unbounded experiment carousel. If it succeeds, Unit 2 may rank one concrete vertical proposal after proving provenance, removable obligations, new overhead and the original product's cold/multiple-root/public-callback/reentry contracts. The later user authorization of plan-led work permits evidence and reviewed bounded implementation; it does not turn diagnostic intervals into causal savings.
